notes.title: Devlog #27: Curiosity Jack
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Martians!  [/h1]  

[b]We’re back with another awesome devlog for you! [/b]

This time we’d like to talk about fixing Curiosity Rover. As you know from the previous post, our Curiosity consists of [b]1387[/b] components, including screws and other small elements. But tinkering with those parts will be different than dismantling components from MER Twins or Sojourner Rover. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/f97ad27b500c6188aedb479f857eaf5c36592bc4.png[/img]

Since the Curiosity Rover is a car-sized vehicle, you have to use a different type of jack in order to make repairs. Besides, the rover’s internal components have to be dismantled from the bottom, so our design team has to design a jack that allows you to work underneath the vehicle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/0b84d6ae987d35448bd2de67a2da6291d754b576.png[/img]

Our 3d graphic designers modelled the jack based on the reference photos they had priorly collected (mostly from NASA JPL website). Below you can take a look at some of these pictures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/86b7b51e32c3044e7768f89acba2e29e2846f418.png[/img]
[i](Image: © NASA/JPL-Caltech)[/i]

Given the size and weight of new rovers, the original Curiosity jack is a fixed-height structure that lets engineers from JPL and NASA crawl under the vehicle, similar to what you might see in regular car workshops. To make the digital jack fit RMS gameplay-wise, our developers slightly redesigned the jack to make it height-adjustable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/f4831a6d5dd56d0d1562dd1387d4f9ba21939e81.png[/img]

We're working hard on Curiosity Rover Update, which will add the big rover and additional hours of gameplay. Stay tuned and feel free to join our [url=https://discord.gg/wK9TGPe]Discord server[/url]! Remember also to follow our upcoming game [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/]Occupy Mars: The game[/url] and add it to your Wishlist.

notes.title: Devlog #17: Assembly, Disassembly and Analysis of Mars Exploration Rover Model
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/u9E57y4.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Dear Martians![/b][/h1]

[b]Making repairs of Mars rovers will involve working in three modes: the assembly mode, the disassembly mode and the analysis mode.[/b] You will need to employ these modes while using the circuits workbench and optical workbench or while working directly on Mars rovers. In each case, the modes you’ll use will be the same, the only difference will lie in the type of the joining elements you’ll need to remove to disassemble a given part, such as screws, solder alloys, etc. Today’s devlog will focus on the assembly, disassembly and analysis of the [b]Mars Exploration Rover model[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/NDP6ldb.png[/img]

[h1]Disassembly mode[/h1]
This mode will be used to remove components from the rover. When you right-click some part of the vehicle, the display will focus on that part and you’ll be able to freely rotate the camera around it. In the bottom right corner of the screen, you’ll see information related to that element (name, image and wear level). If it’s possible to disassemble the part and you hold the right mouse button, it will unlock the screws and cables that will need to be removed in order to detach the component. If it’s not possible to disassemble the part, then the components that block the operation and need to be dismantled will light up in red. The removed element will be stored in the player’s inventory, where it can be destroyed (using the recycling machine), or reattached to a suitable place in the rover.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/n8HHZRw.gif[/img]

[h1]Assembly mode[/h1]
In this mode, the parts that can be installed in the rover will be displayed (x-ray images). Camera rotation will work in the same way as in the disassembly mode. After selecting the part that you want to mount, you’ll need to hold the right mouse button. This action will call up a special UI that will let you choose the element you want to attach. Then, the part you selected will appear on the rover and the mode that helps you unfasten the screws and connect the cables will be activated. Once the process is complete, the part will be treated as mounted.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/J6Fjzr1.gif[/img]

[h1]Analysis mode[/h1]
In this mode, you’ll be able to check the wear level of each component. A faulty part should be repaired only if its wear level drops below 35%. While analyzing the parts, camera rotation will work in the same way as in the other modes. A right click on a component will display its state of wear.
The red colour will signify the wear level between 0 and 35%.
The yellow colour will indicate the wear level between 36 and 75%.
The green colour will refer to the wear level between 76 and 100%.
Based on an analysis of the state of wear, you’ll decide which parts you want to repair.

notes.title: Devlog #16: The Workbench
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/RIMMkRN.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Dear Martians! [/b][/h1]

The [b]Workbench[/b] will allow you to repair broken components of the [b]Printed Circuit Boards[/b] (PCB) that are used in [b]Mars rovers[/b]. Each rover is equipped with several boards that consist of different elements (coils, resistors, memory etc.). They are susceptible to damage and if they break, the PCB stops working and it needs to be repaired. You can print a new board with all its components or print individual elements that need to be soldered onto the PCB.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/BhmXD9t.gif[/img]

[b]Repair process:[/b]
Before making repairs, you have to choose the PCB that needs to be fixed. Initially, you don’t get any additional information about the wear levels of specific parts (however, you can guess which parts may be damaged by the appearance of the material). 

[b]The Workbench allows you to work in three modes:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Disassembly mode[/b]: In this mode, you will choose which components you want to disassemble. You must then melt the solder alloy and remove the items from the PCB.

[*] [b]Assembly mode[/b]: In this mode, you can choose which elements you want to mount on the PCB. You must then solder the joints.

[*] [b]Analysis mode[/b]: In this mode, you can check the current state of each component and see if it needs to be repaired. 
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/h0dKCXm.gif[/img]

While using the workbench, the player first enter the analysis mode to identify the faulty components. Once you’ve checked which elements need to be repaired or replaced, you have to print new parts using the [b]3D printer[/b]. In the disassembly mode, you have to remove the damaged components and then in the assembly mode, you will solder new ones onto the PCB.

notes.title: Devlog #11: 3D Printing and Recycling
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/344ddaad770c31d86b33ccf90d6491d2ea8585a1.png[/img]

[h1][b]Dear Martians! [/b][/h1]
 
Making repairs on Mars can be difficult due to limited reserves of spare parts. Since you won’t be able to buy new components or deliver them from Earth, you will have a [b]3D printer[/b] and a [b]recycling machine[/b] at your disposal. 
 
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/e6a0ed41ab23f08b983884c6853095630e7adea5.png[/img]

The [b]3D printer[/b] is a device that allows you to print parts of the rover that need to be replaced. The printing process will cost you an amount of raw materials and will be a bit time-consuming. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/faef814bef44107bbc0f9a3e8faefb2a443df194.png[/img]

[b]3D printing process:[/b]
1. First you open the printer’s menu and select parts that can be printed.
2. You can choose several parts, which will be automatically placed in a queue (max 5 items). The more complicated and valuable the part, the longer the printing process takes. 
3.  While printing, you can for example play a mini-game or do something else to pass the time. The device will be running in the background.
4. The printed parts are placed inside capsules which have to be collected before the items are available in the inventory. When printing is completed, you’ll get a notification. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/4c49cdbea1a0ed32bcdf91b0b90f6c68f04fc3ad.png[/img]

Some of the parts removed from rovers are worthless and can’t be repaired. You can destroy them using a recycling machine. The [b]recycling machine [/b] turns the unusable parts into resources that you can later use in 3D printing. The better the condition of the part, the bigger the amount of raw materials that you obtain. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/af4a268e0b3ecc4df57bc35c2bbf994496fbe347.png[/img]

The recycling machine immediately destroys the parts when you press the “Destroy” button. The components you select are placed in a queue so that you can look through them before clicking “Destroy”.
 
[b]The recycling process: [/b]
1.  Open a special UI which displays all the parts that are in the inventory. 
2.  Choose which components you want to destroy. Similarly to 3D printing, they are placed in a queue (max 5 items). 
3.  When you press the “Destroy” button, the parts get destroyed and you receive a given amount of raw materials.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/91719d2a77a76d49d91f07753ca20077d9663e00.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #8: The Rover's Antennas
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/a17ffd76a4a156bb1470e2545eb27f789718464d.png[/img]

[h1][b]Dear Martians![/b][/h1]

In today's post we would like you to get familiar with [i]Spirit[/i] and [i]Opportunity’s[/i] [b]antennas[/b] that serve as rover’s "voice" and "ears". The rover is equipped with a [b]low-gain[/b] and [b]high-gain antenna[/b] as well as an [b]UHF antenna[/b] that are mounted on the [b]equipment deck[/b].

The [b]low-gain antenna[/b] is a long-range antenna that can transmit and receive information in almost every direction. The antenna sends radio waves at a low rate to the [b]Deep Space Network[/b] (DSN) antennas on Earth.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/e1a6ae4cbc1d80c45e7561ee163e231b7982c1fc.png[/img]

The [b]high-gain antenna[/b] is a long-range antenna that has a capability to transmit an information in a specific direction.The antenna is steerable and can move to point itself directly to [b]Deep Space Network[/b] (DSN) antennas.  

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/2035ae645a9eb04d51b9cb9c7638c9ad964bb8e6.png[/img]

The [b]UHF antenna[/b] (ultra-high frequency antenna)  is a close-range antenna that is used to communicate with Earth through NASA's orbiters around Mars. One [b]UHF antenna[/b] is mounted on the rover and one is on the petal of the lander. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/fb1249f2082aa6cdb0c905156470568f41e2d918.png[/img]

The antennas are a complicated devices that have many tiny elements. These components can be damaged and in that case the antennas won't work properly. Mars rovers without its "ears" and "voice" can't perform their tasks well, so you'll have to repair broken elements.

------

For example, you will have a [b]drill-driver[/b] and [b]riveting tool[/b] at your disposal, which work great on jobs requiring precision.

[b]Drill-driver[/b] - cordless drill that is mainly used for driving fasteners or screws and removing screws. It is also used for tightening nuts and removing the rivets. The device is equipped with adjustable clutch, that allow you to control the level of torque in order to avoid overdriving a screw or fastener or to prevent damaging delicate parts of the rover.

- Cross recessed tip socket;
- Flat tip socket;  
- Hex socket;
- Hex shank;

You can adjust the sockets to the drill-driver, which allow you to fasten screws of various size. Each socket is available in three different size (small, medium, large). The game itself sets the right socket, and the player just adjusts the size to the compatible screw. Additionally, you will have the drill bit, which will allow you to remove the rivets from parts of the rover.

notes.title: Devlog #1: Backstory
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Martians! [/h1]

When NASA announced that the Opportunity Rover mission officially ended on Feb 13th we were all very sad. This "little rover that could" along with his twin brother Spirit landed on Mars in January 2004. 

Since that time he gave us amazing science and pictures. He was designed to operate for 90 days, but he worked tirelessly for 15 years! 

We thought it's not fair that the Rover is to stay broken on Mars forever and we decided that if there's anything we could do to bring him (and other Mars Rovers) back to life we would do it! 

That's why we are announcing Rover Mechanic Simulator - a new game in the "Occupy Mars" Universe where you play as one of the colonists - an engineer who works in one of the first Mars bases with the goal of fixing all the historic Rovers and Landers that ever landed on the Red Planet.

Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Phoenix, InSight and more... all of the rovers and landers that ever touched the surface of the Red Planet we want to ultimately add to this game. Learning all the details about their internal components and hundreds of scientific instruments they have on board will be an exciting and fun scientific adventure!

We know that players who enjoy playing "Mechanic" games usually don't play survival / open-world simulators and we hope that thanks to Rover Mechanic some of you will actually get more interested in Mars exploration as well :) 

Also we want to clarify that by making [i]Rover Mechanic Simulator[/i] we are not taking anything away from Occupy Mars - on the contrary - thanks to this second game we were able to grow our team so we can actually do more in both games.
